about: A ten-minute weekly sync, run as a normal user would. Charlie (the user) is on the microphone; Alice and Bob are remote. One decision, three tasks for two owners, one deadline, one open question, one changed requirement, and plenty of ordinary talk around them.
windowTitle: Customer portal weekly | Meeting | Microsoft Teams

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Hi both, thanks for joining. This is the customer portal weekly.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Hi Alice. Hi Charlie.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Hi everyone. Good to see you.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Let's start with a quick status round, and then we have a few things to settle about the redesign.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Sure. On my side, the new navigation is finished and it is running on the staging site since Monday.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The search page still has a layout problem on small screens, but that is a small fix.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: I spent most of the week on the account settings page. The forms are done, and I started on the error messages.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Great progress. How did the support team like the new navigation?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: They liked it. Their only comment was that the help link is hard to find.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: That matches what I heard from two customers last week.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The staging site is a bit slow on the account pages. The page load is about three seconds.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Is that the database or the front end?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Mostly the front end. The account page loads every widget at once.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: We saw the same thing on the old portal. Lazy loading helped a lot there.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Right, the new code already does lazy loading for images, just not for the widgets.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Is it a problem for the release?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Not really. Three seconds is within our target, but it could be better.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Okay, good to know.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The deployment pipeline is also faster now. A full build takes about twelve minutes instead of twenty.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: That is a nice improvement. It makes testing much less painful.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Is anything blocked at the moment?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: No, nothing is blocked. We are waiting on the final icons from the design team, but they are not needed until next month.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Same for me, nothing blocked.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: I also read the survey results from last month.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Most customers said the old portal was hard to use on a phone.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: That is exactly why the new layout is mobile first.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The mobile numbers are interesting. About sixty percent of visits come from phones now.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: That is much higher than two years ago.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: It used to be around thirty percent, if I remember correctly.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: And most of those visits are people checking their invoices.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Makes sense. Invoices are the most visited page by far.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Good to know. We can look at the help link placement later.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: I also want to show you the new analytics dashboard quickly, if we have a minute.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: This is the weekly view. Visits went up by about eight percent since the new navigation went live on staging.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Is that real users or mostly our own testing?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Good question. It is only internal traffic on staging, so the numbers are not very meaningful yet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Then let's not read too much into them until the release.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Agreed. The more interesting part is the funnel for the checkout.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: About a third of people who start a payment on the old portal stop on the second step.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: The second step is the one that asks for the billing address again, right?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Exactly. The new checkout flow fills it in automatically.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: That alone could make a real difference.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: It is also the part customers mention most in the survey comments.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: That is everything on the dashboard for now.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Thanks, that was useful context.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Now, the first thing to settle. For the redesign, we have been going back and forth between building a new design system and using the one we already have.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: A new design system would give us more freedom, but it would easily take two months before we could use it.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: And the existing one already covers almost every component we need for the portal.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: So I suggest we use the existing design system for the portal.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Agreed, that makes sense to me.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Yes, I agree. Let's go with the existing design system.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Great, that is decided then.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Maybe we should also try a new color palette at some point. The current blue feels a bit dated.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Maybe, but I would not change colors in the middle of the redesign.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Let's leave the colors for another time.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Before the client change, a quick look at the support tickets from last week.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: We had forty two tickets about the portal. That is a bit lower than the week before.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: What were the main topics?

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Mostly password resets, and people who could not find their old invoices.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The invoice search in the new portal should fix most of those.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: I hope so. The password resets are a different story. Those are usually people who forgot which email address they used.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: That is not really something the portal can solve on its own.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: No, but the new login page shows a hint with the first letters of the email address, which already helps a little.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Support also mentioned that the error messages on the old forms were confusing.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: The new forms explain what went wrong next to each field, so that should be better.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Good. I like that the redesign already answers most of what customers complain about.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: It does. The only open topic from support is the help link we talked about earlier.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Next, there is a change from the client. I talked to them yesterday.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: They now want dark mode in the first release. Before, it was planned for later in the year.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Okay, that changes the plan a bit. Dark mode touches every page.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: The existing design system already has dark colors defined, so it is less work than it sounds.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: True. It mostly means testing every page twice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: The release is still planned for the end of next month.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: With dark mode the testing phase gets longer, but I think the date still holds.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: The designers told me the contrast checks for dark mode are fairly quick.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Good. Then nothing changes for the release date.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: One question from my side. Do we still support the old browser versions?

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Only the last two versions of each browser, same as the main website.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Okay, that answers it. Thanks.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Then let's plan for it. Now, the tasks for this week.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Bob, can you update the checkout flow mockups by Thursday? The client wants to see them in the Friday review.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Yes, I'll update the checkout flow mockups by Thursday.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: I will write the accessibility checklist for the new pages.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Perfect, thank you Charlie.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: I'll also set up the usability test sessions with five customers.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Thanks Bob. That is really helpful.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: About the help link, one option is to put it in the top bar.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Another option is a floating button in the corner.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Floating buttons sometimes cover content on phones.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: True. The top bar is probably the safer choice.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: I don't have a strong opinion. Both could work.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: We can look at it again next week, when we have the usability results.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: One thing we still have not figured out. Who approves the new text on the pricing page?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Last time it was marketing, but they changed their team.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: I honestly do not know who owns that now. We need to find out.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: If nobody approves it in time, the pricing page could delay the whole release.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Good point. Let's keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: How was everyone's weekend, by the way?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Quiet. I finally finished the book I started in the summer.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: We went hiking. The weather was perfect for it.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Nice. I mostly stayed home with the kids.

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: By the way, did either of you try the new coffee place downstairs?

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: I did. The coffee is good, but the line is long in the morning.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Ha, I will try it tomorrow. Okay, anything else for today?

lines.speaker: Bob
lines.text: Nothing from me.

lines.speaker: Charlie
lines.text: Nothing else from me either.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Then thanks everyone, see you next week.

lines: Option A: build a new one (about 2 months)
Option B: use the existing one
Was planned for later in the year
